article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 60% Indica / 40% Sativa
Genetics: Strawberry Banana × Papaya
Breeder: Oni Seed Co.
THC Content: 20–29%
CBD Content: Low to trace
Terpene Profile: Beta-myrcene , limonene , beta-caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Strawberry, guava, papaya, tropical fruit
Flowering Time (Indoor): 63–70 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: early to mid-October
Indoor Yield: High
Outdoor Yield: High
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Strawberry Guava is a cannabis strain built around resin and flavor rather than a catchy fruit name applied after the fact. Oni Seed Co. created the cultivar by combining a selected Strawberry Banana with its prized Papaya mother, producing flowers that can move from strawberry yogurt and tropical smoothie sweetness into ripe guava, melon, candy, Kush, and an unusual funky-fruit finish. Oni’s own company profile identifies Strawberry Guava as Crockett’s Strawberry Banana selection crossed with Papaya and notes that the cultivar earned second place for Best Non-Solvent and first place for highest terpene content at the 2017 Chalice competition.

Those awards help explain why the strain became so closely associated with hash makers. Heavy resin production coats the flowers, while the tropical aromatics survive extraction particularly well. Potency can be substantial too: a 2025 laboratory-tested Strawberry Guava flower sample reached 28.62% total THC. For consumers, the result is flavorful weed that begins with cheerful cerebral energy before developing a warmer, more relaxed physical character.
Genetics and Lineage

The original Strawberry Guava genetics are Strawberry Banana × Papaya, bred by Oni Seed Co. The Strawberry Banana parent was a selected Crockett Family Farms line chosen for its intense strawberry-and-banana aroma, resin coverage, and vigorous growth. Oni’s Papaya mother provides the tropical half of the equation and traces to Mango #33 × Afghani #1. Oni Seed Co.’s CannaCon breeder profile confirms the Strawberry Banana × Papaya pairing and specifically identifies Strawberry Guava as one of the company’s award-winning creations.

Looking deeper into those parents explains why the finished marijuana has such an unusual mixture of confectionery sweetness and ripe-fruit funk. Strawberry Banana contributes creamy strawberry, banana, Kush undertones, and an almost yogurt-like quality. The Papaya side supplies mango, melon, papaya, tropical fruit, and a noticeably heavier Afghani foundation. When the two meet, the aroma can suggest guava even though guava itself does not appear anywhere in the family tree. The name describes the sensory result rather than one of the parents.

The lineage also helped make Strawberry Guava valuable beyond its own flower. Its combination of resin output and aromatic intensity has made the cultivar attractive in hash-oriented breeding, where preserving terpene quality through solventless extraction matters as much as flower appearance. That breeding value is part of the reason the genetics continue to appear in modern crosses long after many fruit-heavy strains from the same era faded from attention.
Effects and Experience

The opening stage of Strawberry Guava tends to be considerably brighter than its indica-leaning classification might imply. Mood elevation can appear quickly, accompanied by a more playful or creative mental state. Proper Cannabis, which grows the Oni Seed Co. genetics, characterizes the experience as uplifted, euphoric, and creative. Music, casual conversation, art, gaming, cooking, and other relaxed activities can fit well during this portion of the high because the cerebral effects generally appear before substantial body heaviness.

As the experience continues, the Papaya and Afghani side of the genetic background becomes more noticeable. Physical tension can begin to soften, movement feels less urgent, and the initial mental enthusiasm settles into a calmer state. Moderate amounts may remain social and functional for experienced consumers, whereas larger servings can become considerably more sedating. This progression gives Strawberry Guava broader appeal than cannabis that immediately produces either intense stimulation or couch-lock.

Potency varies considerably by grower and phenotype. A Rhize Cannabis flower sample tested in September 2025 contained 28.617% calculated total THC and 33.788% total cannabinoids, with CBD below quantifiable levels. At that strength, inexperienced consumers should approach the cultivar cautiously. Excessive THC can lead to dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, short-term concentration problems, increased heart rate, or anxiety even when the normal experience is relaxed and euphoric.
Medical Benefits

Strawberry Guava may appeal to medical marijuana consumers who prefer a strain capable of improving mood without immediately producing strong lethargy. Some patients select similar indica-leaning hybrids when temporary stress, low appetite, physical tension, or discomfort becomes distracting. The cerebral portion of the experience may make moderate servings more practical earlier in the evening, while stronger doses can shift toward deeper physical relaxation.

Terpene composition varies between harvests, but several cultivators working with authenticated Strawberry Guava genetics show recurring chemistry. Wojo Co. identifies beta-caryophyllene, beta-myrcene, beta-pinene, limonene, and linalool in its Strawberry Guava material, while Proper Cannabis lists myrcene, limonene, and caryophyllene as prominent terpenes. Together, these compounds fit the strain’s combination of ripe fruit, citrus brightness, peppery spice, herbs, and softer floral notes.

Those aromatic compounds should not be interpreted as proof that Strawberry Guava treats anxiety, depression, chronic pain, insomnia, or another medical condition. The cultivar itself has not undergone clinical trials establishing strain-specific therapeutic benefits. Medical consumers should rely on laboratory testing for the particular cannabis product they purchase and consider their individual THC tolerance, medications, and healthcare guidance.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Strawberry Guava’s aroma is unusually faithful to its name. Strawberry appears quickly when the flowers are opened, but the character is richer than fresh berries alone. Creaminess inherited from Strawberry Banana can make the aroma resemble strawberry yogurt or a fruit smoothie, while Papaya contributes ripe tropical fruit, melon, and a heavier sweetness. Once the flower is broken apart, the profile becomes increasingly exotic, developing guava, candy, herbs, and occasional funky or almost overripe-fruit notes.

Wojo Co., which identifies its Strawberry Guava genetics as Strawberry Banana × Papaya bred by Oni Seed Co., highlights candy sweetness and guava with floral nuances. Proper Cannabis similarly describes strawberry, cream, and sweetness as central characteristics. Neither description fully captures the stranger backend, however. Well-preserved phenotypes can develop mild cheese-like funk, Kush, spearmint-like freshness, or fermented tropical fruit beneath the brighter flavors.

The inhale often begins with strawberry and sweet tropical fruit. Guava and papaya become more obvious across the middle of the palate, followed by cream, Kush, and a mildly funky finish. A careful cure is especially important with this weed because its lighter strawberry and tropical aromatics are volatile. Overly warm drying conditions can leave the flower sweet but eliminate much of the complexity that made the genetics famous among extractors.
Growing Information

Strawberry Guava is a photoperiod cultivar that generally finishes after approximately 63–70 days of flowering. Growers should expect substantial vigor from the Strawberry Banana side, including strong branching and enough stretch that indoor height should be planned before flowering begins. The Papaya parent helps reinforce production, and the original breeder description emphasizes both large yields and exceptionally heavy resin development.

Topping during vegetative growth can help transform the plant’s vertical energy into a wider canopy. Low-stress training and trellising are also useful because productive branches can become increasingly heavy once flowers begin stacking. Interior growth that receives little light can be selectively removed before late bloom, improving airflow while concentrating resources around better-developed tops. Strawberry Guava is particularly attractive to growers interested in solventless extraction because the flowers can produce abundant trichomes with strongly preserved tropical terpenes. Wojo describes its selection as an extractor-oriented plant with impressive resin and hash production.

Humidity control becomes important as the resinous flowers gain density. Constant airflow through the canopy reduces moisture pockets, while avoiding excessive humidity late in bloom helps protect mature buds. Outdoors, plants perform best with abundant sunlight and enough autumn warmth to accommodate roughly nine to ten weeks of flowering. Early-to-mid-October is a practical planning range in many Northern Hemisphere climates, although trichome development and flower maturity should determine the actual harvest date.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Strawberry Guava?
Strawberry Guava is Strawberry Banana × Papaya. Oni Seed Co. confirms that the Strawberry Banana parent was a selected Crockett line and that its Papaya mother was used to create the original cross.
Who bred Strawberry Guava?

Oni Seed Co. bred the original Strawberry Guava. The cultivar became one of the company’s signature hash-oriented genetics after winning second place for Best Non-Solvent and first place for highest terpene content at the 2017 Chalice competition.
Is Strawberry Guava indica or sativa?

The original cultivar is generally described as approximately 60% indica and 40% sativa. Its effects reflect that balance, beginning with euphoric cerebral activity before gradually becoming more physically relaxing.
How strong is Strawberry Guava?

Potency depends on phenotype and cultivation, but high-quality examples can reach the upper-20% THC range. A laboratory-tested 2025 flower sample measured 28.617% total THC with CBD below quantifiable levels.
What does Strawberry Guava taste like?

Expect strawberry, guava, papaya, tropical fruit, sweet candy, and creamy flavors, sometimes accompanied by Kush, herbs, flowers, or funky overripe-fruit notes. Proper Cannabis highlights strawberry, cream, and sweetness, while Wojo emphasizes candy and guava aromatics.
Final Thoughts on Strawberry Guava

Strawberry Guava earned its reputation through characteristics that matter well beyond dispensary shelf appeal. Oni Seed Co. paired a selected Strawberry Banana with Papaya and produced cannabis capable of combining heavy resin output, vigorous production, substantial potency, and a genuinely distinctive tropical terpene profile . Its success at the 2017 Chalice competition—second in Best Non-Solvent and first for terpene content—demonstrated early on that the genetics were especially well suited to hash production.

For flower consumers, however, extraction performance is only part of the story. Strawberry yogurt, guava, papaya, tropical candy, cream, Kush, and occasional funky fruit create a flavor profile with far more depth than a simple berry strain. The high follows a similarly layered path, beginning euphoric and mentally engaging before becoming increasingly relaxed through the body. For cannabis enthusiasts who value fruit-forward weed but want authentic breeder history, serious resin production, and a flavor profile proven in solventless competition, Strawberry Guava remains one of Oni Seed Co.’s most important creations.
